source.title: Investigating Memorization in Language Models Trained via Knowledge Distillation

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies memorization under knowledge distillation, not scaling laws or their predictions. It cites scaling work in the introduction but does not test or rely on the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions that generative capabilities scale with model size and training tokens, citing prior work, but reports no scaling-law fit, size/token/compute sweep, extrapolation test, or compute-optimal allocation. It does report a cross-entropy comparison on Dforget under different teacher-training data conditions; this is recorded under fits_no_version because it does not test any claim version.
record.test_reason: The study examines memorization under knowledge distillation with Pythia 160M/410M/1B teachers. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only in the introduction and reports no loss-vs-scale fit, extrapolation, allocation, architecture-shape or downstream-scaling result. Three model sizes are used only as teacher-size conditions for memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that knowledge distillation reduces memorization when teacher and student see different data, but teachers leak memorized content. They find it accelerates memorization when the student trains on sequences the teacher memorized, and accelerates forgetting. Teacher size trades off how fast memorized content transfers against how much the student memorizes. They draw no scaling-law conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines memorization during knowledge distillation and does not apply the scaling-law methods or fitting procedures in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Memorization outcomes vary with teacher size and whether the student, teacher, or both were trained on the injected sequences.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher cross-entropy on Dforget differs by under 0.001 nats between teachers trained on Dinject and on Dplain, at all three sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injecting 20 sequences repeated 200 times (<0.2% of data) has negligible effect on held-out language-modelling loss.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC 2026)
record.problems: The study does not provide evidence on the listed scaling-law claims; its models and experiments address memorization under knowledge distillation instead.

untested.parts: No loss vs parameters/tokens/compute relationship is reported.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
No scaling-law form in other modalities or regimes. Distillation is studied for memorization only.
No fitting choices or exponent comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The teacher-size effects concern memorization, not pretraining loss scaling, so they bear on no version. The record's T6/cites_only classification is correct.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law loss relationship across parameters, tokens, or compute is tested.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs is tested.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is tested.
No scaling-law test in other modalities or training regimes is conducted.
No downstream-task predictability from scale or pretraining loss is tested.
No scaling-law fitting choices, exponent disagreements, or curve bending are investigated.
